## Scope and data

This report summarizes the November 9, 2026 analysis snapshot for a synthetic product dataset of 5,000 users across 12 signup cohorts. It is not real customer data.

**Provenance note:** The original saved outputs and this report disagree on session volume, conversion, month-6 retention, and model AUC. The corrected branch contains focused methodological scripts, but not a complete committed pipeline that regenerates every value below. Values are therefore identified as report-reported results, not independently reproduced outputs.

## Conversion funnel

| Stage | Users | Share of signups |
|---|---:|---:|
| Signup | 5,000 | 100.00% |
| Onboarding | 3,874 | 77.48% |
| Activation | 2,407 | 48.14% |
| Engagement | 1,387 | 27.74% |
| Conversion | 647 | 12.94% |

The largest absolute loss occurs between signup and onboarding (1,126 users); activation is also a substantial drop-off. Funnel percentages are calculated against the signup population in the report.

## Cohort retention and engagement

The report-reported month-6 retention is 1,563 of 5,000 users (31.26%). This is a descriptive result from the synthetic dataset. A higher retention rate among a behaviorally defined segment would not, by itself, establish that the segment definition or its behaviors caused retention.

## Predictive baseline

The report describes a logistic-regression model using first-month features, evaluated on 1,001 test users.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| ROC-AUC | 0.567 |
| Precision | 0.406 |
| Recall | 0.329 |
| Specificity | 0.781 |
| Accuracy | 0.639 |
| Threshold | 0.346 |

The ROC-AUC indicates weak ranking discrimination. The model is a baseline demonstration and should not be presented as a high-performing retention model.

## Simulated onboarding experiment

The experiment is separate from the 5,000-user product simulation and has 1,251 simulated users per arm.

| Period | Treatment-control difference | One-sided p-value |
|---|---:|---:|
| Weeks 1-2 | +5.116 percentage points | <0.001 |
| Weeks 3-4 | +1.199 percentage points | 0.143 |

The experiment generates outcomes from assumed probabilities. These figures demonstrate a statistical testing workflow; they are not observed product outcomes or evidence of a real intervention effect. The early-versus-late difference should not be described as an empirically established novelty effect.

## Limitations

- Synthetic data only. Results do not establish performance on a real consumer product.
- The current committed corrected scripts do not regenerate the full report snapshot end to end.
- Earlier saved outputs differ from this report on session volume, conversion, month-6 retention, and ROC-AUC.
- The prediction model has modest discrimination.
- The A/B exercise is a separate simulation with assumed probabilities, not a live or historical randomized experiment.
- DAU/MAU and cohort summaries depend on the synthetic observation-window construction.

## Reproducibility status

The original scripts remain in `scripts/`; audited focused scripts remain in `corrected_r/scripts/`. See `corrected_r/README.md` for the scripts currently available and the safeguards they implement. Do not treat the report-reported figures as regenerated until a complete pipeline and its generated outputs are committed and checked.
